findings.claim: In the search window, a typed query that becomes impossible and then possible again turns the launcher's data hooks off and back on. That re-requests pins, collections, Smart Collections, the missing count, auth status, the flat folder tree and the tag list, for a query that holds new tokens and no in: or -in: name.
findings.impact: Typing an exclusion whose value has the same name as a positive tag along the way (e.g. 'tag:trip -tag:trip2023' passes through 'tag:trip -tag:trip') makes the window reload /collections and /smart-folders. It also reloads the whole flat folder tree (up to 50,000 entries) on every keystroke that leaves the impossible state. Results are not wrong; the cost is extra load and network traffic in a surface that I20 says loads no list for such a query.
findings.evidence: useLauncherRows.ts:47-59 passes `open && !scope && !impossible` as `active` to useJumpDestinations, useJumpFolders and useDriveTagNames. useJumpDestinations.ts:77-90 (useDriveOwned) re-runs `load(drive)` whenever `active` goes from false to true, and useIsAdmin (:97-110) refetches as well. Before the change `active` stayed true for the whole time the window was open. GlobalSearch.negation.test.tsx only asserts that the impossible query itself sends no /collections request, not what happens on the transition back.
findings.repro: Open the search window on a drive and type 'tag:trip -tag:trip', then append '2023'. Reading the code, after the last keystroke the window sends GET /collections, /smart-folders, /pins, the folder tree (flat), tags, summary and auth status again. Not run.

bucket_proposal.reason: I20: a query with no in: or -in: name, whatever new tokens it holds, loads no list. Here the window loads the collection and Smart Collection lists again because of such a query (I28 also limits when the Smart Collection list is requested).

findings.proposed_fix: Keep `active` tied to `open && !scope` for the data hooks and apply `impossible` only to `off` (hiding the rows), so an impossible query hides rows without unloading and reloading the data.

findings.claim: On the search page, an in: query whose in: key does not change is resolved again (lists reloaded, and its in: Smart Collection evaluated again with a new `now`) after the query passes through an impossible state and back, because the resolution effect depends on `impossible` and clears the held resolution.
findings.impact: For a submitted 'in:Weekly tag:x -tag:x' followed by removing the '-tag:x' chip, the page reloads both lists and evaluates Weekly again, although the in: key is the same. A Weekly with a relative modified: can then list a slightly different member set. The window (useFileSearch) keeps its held resolution in the same sequence, so the page and the window behave differently.
findings.evidence: useFolderFiles.ts:291-296 sets the resolution to null when `impossible`, and :333 lists `impossible` in the effect deps, so a false->true->false flip of `impossible` with an unchanged inKey starts a new resolveInNames at :309 with modifiedNowRef.current, a new run's `now` (:184-191). useFileSearch.ts:123-134 returns early without touching resolutionRef, and :209-210 reuses the held resolution when the listKey matches.
findings.repro: Render FolderBrowser with searchQuery 'in:"Weekly" tag:x', wait for the evaluation, rerender with 'in:"Weekly" tag:x -tag:x', then with 'in:"Weekly" tag:x'. Reading the code, the evaluation listing for Weekly is sent a second time. Not run.

bucket_proposal.reason: I28: only a change of the in: key, 再試行 or a reload resolves again, and a q change does not. I29 holds the Smart Collection's `now` until the in: key changes.

findings.proposed_fix: While impossible, stop requesting but keep the held resolution (or key the held resolution by inKey and reuse it when `impossible` clears), as useFileSearch does.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: The search window hides jump rows and suggestions for a query that is impossible by kinds or conditions, but not for one that is impossible by range (useLauncherRows omits hasImpossibleRange), while the window's listing treats all three alike.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Typing 'size:>1GB size:<1MB' in the window still shows jump rows while results are empty, whereas 'tag:x -tag:x' hides them, an inconsistency the user may notice.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: The window's search cache is keyed by the query text, so an entry written before this change for a query such as '京都 -tag:x' (then searched as text) can be read for the same text after it.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: It needs a cache entry that survives the deploy for exactly that text; the user would briefly see the stale text-search results until revalidation.

regression_risks: useDriveOwned refetches on every inactive-to-active flip, so any future condition added to the launcher's `active` multiplies requests for the folder tree.
The resolution effect in useFolderFiles now depends on `impossible`, so any future impossibility rule also discards and recomputes in: resolutions.
